claims.claim: A phase III trial of teriparatide in elderly women with at least one vertebral fracture showed significant reductions in vertebral and appendicular fracture rates, without evidence of superiority to bisphosphonates.
claims.episode_span: significant reductions in both vertebral and appendicular fracture rates.
claims.source_title: Parathyroid hormone and teriparatide for the treatment of osteoporosis: a review of the evidence and suggested guidelines for its use
claims.supporting_quote: Significant reductions in both vertebral and appendicular fracture rates have been demonstrated in the phase III trial of teriparatide, involving elderly women with at least one prevalent vertebral fracture before the onset of therapy.

claims.claim: The 2005 review said teriparatide is not recommended for more than two years, based in part on osteosarcoma in a rat carcinogenicity model.
claims.episode_span: teriparatide is not recommended for more than two years, based in part on osteosarcoma in a rat carcinogenicity model.
claims.source_title: Parathyroid hormone and teriparatide for the treatment of osteoporosis: a review of the evidence and suggested guidelines for its use
claims.supporting_quote: Teriparatide therapy is not recommended for more than 2 yr, based, in part, on the induction of osteosarcoma in a rat model of carcinogenicity.

claims.claim: A 2016 review said daily teriparatide increases bone formation more than resorption through remodeling-based and modeling-based formation and more new remodeling sites, and that clinical use is limited to 24 months.
claims.episode_span: teriparatide appears to increase bone formation more than bone resorption, on biochemical markers and on histology.
claims.source_title: Teriparatide for osteoporosis: importance of the full course
claims.supporting_quote: The use of teriparatide clinically is limited to 24 months.

claims.claim: A 2005 health-technology assessment included 90 randomized trials and found vertebral-fracture reductions for five named drugs including teriparatide, with no direct comparison showing one significantly more effective, and cost-per-QALY estimates of £35,000 thresholds by age.
claims.episode_span: A 2005 Health Technology Assessment systematic review included 90 randomized controlled trials
claims.source_title: A systematic review and economic evaluation of alendronate, etidronate, risedronate, raloxifene and teriparatide for the prevention and treatment of postmenopausal osteoporosis
claims.supporting_quote: Ninety randomised controlled trials (RCTs) met the inclusion criteria.

claims.claim: Mouse exosomes carrying teriparatide mRNA increased cellular teriparatide production and osteogenic readouts, bound bone, and showed bone fluorescence for at least 72 hours after intravenous injection.
claims.episode_span: bone-associated fluorescence remained detectable for at least 72 hours
claims.source_title: Bone-targeting engineered exosomes delivering teriparatide mRNA for the treatment of osteoporosis
claims.supporting_quote: Following systemic administration, bone-associated fluorescence remained detectable for at least 72 h, with greater femoral and tibial fluorescence and lower relative hepatic fluorescence than those observed with unmodified exosomes.

claims.claim: A case report described a contralateral impending atypical femoral fracture after a single denosumab dose in a bisphosphonate-pretreated patient with incomplete teriparatide therapy, despite normal contralateral imaging at the index fracture.
claims.episode_span: a contralateral impending atypical femoral fracture after one dose of denosumab despite a radiologically normal opposite femur at the index fracture.
claims.source_title: Contralateral atypical femoral fracture following a single dose of denosumab after incomplete teriparatide therapy in a patient with long-term bisphosphonate exposure: A case report
claims.supporting_quote: This case demonstrates that contralateral impending AFF can develop after a single dose of denosumab in a bisphosphonate-pretreated patient, despite confirmed radiological normality at the time of the index fracture.
